record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.original_question: If supersymmetry is broken in a hidden sector, the visible Standard Model sector must still acquire soft masses that violate the tree-level supertrace relation without reintroducing unacceptable flavor violation. By what channel does the visible sector learn that supersymmetry has been broken—supergravity mediation through Planck-suppressed operators, gauge mediation through loops of messenger fields, pseudo-anomalous U(1) mediation, or another mechanism—and what experimental signatures can distinguish the mediation mechanism?

evidence.quote: Question #7 Once SUSY is broken, how do we find out?
We have said that the dynamics of SUSY-breaking must occur far from the sector of the SM. But this begs the question: how does the SM ‘learn’ that SUSY has been broken?
Two routes therefore seem open to us for communicating SUSY-breaking to the visible sector: loops and non-renormalizable interactions. Both have found application in realistic models.

Can experiments differentiate this type of mediation from supergravity mediation? Perhaps most significantly for phenomenology, these models predict that the lightest SUSY particle will be the gravitino and that other SUSY particles can decay into it with observable lifetimes.

artifact.status_search_result: As of 2026, no superpartners have been observed at the LHC or any other experiment, so the empirical question of which mediation mechanism (if any) is realized in nature remains open. Theoretical model-building has produced detailed predictions for gravity, gauge, anomaly, and U(1) mediation scenarios, and characteristic signatures (e.g., gravitino LSP with NLSP decays for gauge mediation) are well understood, but the lack of a discovered SUSY spectrum prevents experimental discrimination.

status_evidence.title: ATLAS SUSY searches summary
status_evidence.snippet: No significant excess observed; limits set on sparticle masses across a variety of mediation scenarios.
status_evidence.claim: Supersymmetric particles have not been discovered, so the mediation mechanism cannot yet be experimentally identified.
